[ISSUE backstage/backstage#30607 by Teo-ShaoWei] Migrate to Zod 4
### 📜 Issue Labels

- [x] Please familiarize yourself with the issue labels used in this project: [LABELS.md](https://github.com/backstage/backstage/blob/master/LABELS.md)

### 🔎 Search Terms

```

### 🗃️ Project Area

Unknown

### 🛠️ Task

We are to upgrade Zod 3 (i.e. `zod@^3.22.4`) to Zod 4. As a result, we should upgrade `zod-validation-error@^3.4.0` to at least `zod-validation-error@^3.5.0` for [Zod 4 support](https://github.com/causaly/zod-validation-error/releases/tag/v3.5.0).

We will want to replace all usage of `zod-to-json-schema` with [native Zod 4 JSON schema support](https://zod.dev/json-schema).

Need be, we can ignore the following package versions that are in use:
- `zod@^3.23.8`, which is a nested dependency of the MCP/OpenAI external dependencies only.
- `zod-validation-error@^3.0.3` as that is a nested dependency of `knip` only.

### 📊 Priority & Impact

Zod 4 is faster, smaller, and supports JSON schema compared to Zod 3. Details in their documentation [Introducing Zod 4](https://zod.dev/v4).

Zod is mostly used locally to verify the type of the received unstructured object. Cross-package coupling would likely be due to backend/frontend of the same plugin family. Caution should especially be taken if a package import types from Zod, which likely mean it's dependent on another package that create objects of these types. With care, it is likely possible to upgrade to Zod 4 iteratively and independently.

Since refactoring of overall code design might be hard after the code takes shape, so this might be a good time to do some simple design maintenance. For example, complete the export and usage of `ZodFunctionSchema` from `scaffolder-node` so that most backend plugin modules can import that instead of `zod`.

Yes, but I would like some more guidance
[ISSUE COMMENT by Teo-ShaoWei] I can figure out what needs to be changed and would be glad to contribute. However, I hope to receive guidance on how to manage deprecation in Backstage for such an upgrade 🙏 It can either be from a discussion here, or more eyeball of the PRs I will raise.
[ISSUE COMMENT by GabDug] There's some helpful documentation on [how to support both v3 and v4](https://zod.dev/library-authors#how-to-support-zod-3-and-zod-4-simultaneously).  I've been using /v4 in one of our internal plugin, with zod 3.25, and have had no specific issues.

I guess we could start by setting zod dependency to "^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0" and changing our imports in bulk to `import { z } from 'zod/v3';`.

We can then move on to packages that accept user (plugin) schemas like the scaffolder, which might require more careful efforts. We'll be able to [determine the version of the zod schema](https://zod.dev/library-authors?id=how-to-support-zod-3-and-zod-4-simultaneously) that is passed to us.

I'd be happy to help @Teo-ShaoWei!
[ISSUE COMMENT by Teo-ShaoWei] Thanks @GabDug 🙏 Let's plan and execute this 💪

> There's some helpful documentation on [how to support both v3 and v4](https://zod.dev/library-authors#how-to-support-zod-3-and-zod-4-simultaneously).

Regarding the above suggestion, it might not be applicable for our case since we are not designing tooling on top of Zod. It's also written within that doc:

> This page is primarily intended for consumption by library authors who are building tooling on top of Zod.

For our case, I would believe that we can directly use Zod 4 for those packages that don't further expose it... what do we think?

I would agree with you that the scaffolder case can consider supporting both v3 and v4 👍 The method suggested above doesn't work unfortunately: there are no `schema._zod.def;` to check.  Because we are exposing a `z => schema` function, the content of `z` is not supplied by the user.

Going along that line, if we intend not to break existing schemas, we might have to expose a way to indicate version together with that `z => schema` function, e.g.:
```ts
schema: {
  version: 'zod@4',
  input: {
    values: z =>
      z.record(z.string(), {
        description: 'Values stored as variables for reuse.',
      }),
  },
  output: {
    values: z =>
      z
        .record(z.string())
        .describe('The exact same stored values in input.'),
  },
},
```
Then the scaffolder will check for `schema.version` to determine the correct v3 or v4 `z` to pass through the `z => schema` function. The scaffolder can also write a deprecation message when it cannot find `version: 'zod@4'`...

Considering the templates are owned by devs who might not be Backstage operators in their respective organization, I would agree some deprecation runway might be essential... Not sure how best... 🤔
[ISSUE COMMENT by Teo-ShaoWei] I'm sorry, I stand corrected. There are some functions, like `createSignInResolverFactory`, that receive user schema(s). For those, indeed we can support Zod 3 and 4 using the method suggested above to help user transit to Zod 4.

I'll give it a try and see 💪

Zod is nicely design really. Their v3 and v4 both contain both version of code for now. That way, step (2.) can be done iteratively. That would also be the place where we will likely spend more effort on.

### Component(s)

processor/transform

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently, it is inconvenient to ingest ELF (Extended Log Format) logs because they require complex parsing using non-performant regex. The overhead introduced by this parsing is prohibitive for users trying to work with a well-defined, common format.
Documentation for ELF can be found [here](https://www.w3.org/TR/WD-logfile.html)

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add a new function `parse_elf` to the transform processor's internal set of parsing functions. Its implementation will follow the approach used for the `parse_leef` function. I will implement this function, and the other code owner for the `logparsingfuncs` directory will review it.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

As discussed in issue #44908, we had originally planned to make this an OTTL function, but decided against it for these parsers.

- The internal directory referenced in this issue has yet to be merged (Dir PR -> #48323).

title: [processor/schema] Add cache_ttl configuration option for in-memory schema cache
review: BODY: I am going to say that having a ttl cache is overkill here considering that schemas are immutable, and invalidating the cache here is going to cause either another disk read, or http request would can be costly when multiplied by several thousand deployed instances.
request:
[ISSUE open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib#48342 by MikeGoldsmith] feat(processor/schema): add cache TTL configuration option
### Component(s)

processor/schema

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The schema processor's in-memory cache (`CacheableProvider`) uses `cache.NoExpiration` — entries live forever for the process lifetime. This means:

- If a schema URL initially returns incorrect or empty content, the bad result is cached permanently until the collector restarts.
- If a schema file is updated on the server, the collector won't pick up the new version until restart.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `cache_ttl` configuration option that controls how long successfully fetched schemas are kept in the cache before being re-fetched. The underlying `go-cache` library already supports TTL natively, so this should be a straightforward change for the in-memory layer.

```yaml
processors:
  schema:
    cache_ttl: 24h  # default: no expiration (current behavior)
    targets:
      - https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.26.0
```

#### Interaction with persistent storage (#48267)

When the optional storage extension is configured, the provider chain is: **in-memory cache → storage → HTTP**. A TTL on the in-memory cache alone is insufficient — when an in-memory entry expires, the `StorageProvider` returns the persisted schema before HTTP is reached, effectively making the TTL a periodic re-read from disk rather than a re-fetch from the server.

The implementation should ensure that when the in-memory TTL expires, the collector attempts an HTTP fetch rather than just reloading from storage. Storage should act as a fallback when HTTP fails (offline resilience), not as a permanent override that prevents re-fetching.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- Restarting the collector to clear the cache — works but disruptive.
- No change — schemas rarely change in practice, but having a TTL provides a safety net for misconfigured URLs or updated schema files.
- TTL on in-memory only, accept that storage bypasses it — simpler but the TTL becomes meaningless when storage is configured.

### Additional context

Raised during review of #48267 (storage extension support).

# Megatron-LM Monthly Activity Report — September 2026 (Final, through September 30, 2026)

> Chinese version: [中文版本](https://github.com/lhb8125/megatron-lm-activity-report/blob/main/reports/zh-CN/2026/09.md)

> Reporting window: 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30 (Asia/Shanghai); source: [`NVIDIA/Megatron-LM`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM).

## Overview

Delivered work advanced DeepSeek-V4 and hybrid-model execution, MFSDP and parallel training, MoE and quantization support, inference serving, multimodal SFT, and checkpoint reliability. Ongoing work advances hybrid model architectures, sparse attention, distributed execution, checkpoint portability, CUDA Graph and offload paths, MoE and MTP efficiency, quantization, inference, and determinism.

- Substantive PR activity after filtering: opened 592; merged 291; closed without merge 179; active at cutoff 392.
- Excluded from the report and statistics: test-only 50, CI-only 25, test/CI-only 6, format-only 0.

## Delivered

### DeepSeek-V4 sparse attention and CSA

DeepSeek-V4 received native hybrid attention construction, compact DSA indexing, fused CSA execution, packed-THD support, and deterministic sparse-attention behavior.

- Added compact cuDNN DSA indexing, load-balanced context-parallel indexing, and plan-driven packed-THD scoring with reusable layout metadata. ([dev #5992](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/5992), [dev #6058](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6058), [dev #6206](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6206))
- Added DeepSeek-V4 HybridModel construction and orchestration for compressed, windowed, sink, and D2 attention patterns, including fused SBHD CSA execution and an Agent Compose path using Core fusions, THD attention projection, main-gradient accumulation, and overlapped collectives. ([main #6402](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6402), [main #6404](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6404), [main #6405](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6405), [dev #7127](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7127))
- Optimized CSA backward and packed-THD training by recomputing inverse RoPE and fusing layout lowering, position mapping, indexer preparation, compressor preparation, and sparse-loss processing. ([dev #7036](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7036), [dev #7064](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7064))
- Stabilized fused CSA Top-K ordering and context-parallel padding behavior for deterministic rollout and policy-loss comparisons. ([dev #7169](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7169))

### MFSDP v2 sharding, scheduling, and MXFP8

MFSDP v2 expanded its scheduling, virtual-pipeline, sharding, accumulation, and MXFP8 capabilities.

- Exposed MFSDP v2 lifecycle controls and integrated shared contexts across virtual pipeline chunks, allowing external schedules and VPP execution to coordinate unshard, reshard, prefetch, gradients, and optimizer handling. ([main #6484](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6484), [main #6486](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6486))
- Added mixed dense and expert sharding strategies, hybrid FSDP bucket formation, fine-grained 1F1B integration, and correct microbatch accumulation behavior. ([main #6594](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6594), [main #6773](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6773), [main #7112](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7112), [main #7186](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7186))

## Scope and Method

The narrative is grouped by technical theme rather than PR chronology. Related `dev` and `main` PRs are described once. The rebuildable raw ledger, exclusion evidence, commit activity, and state events are retained in the workflow database artifact. PRs closed without merge are counted but not narrated. Each PR citation identifies its target branch. Open PRs do not carry into a new month without code or state activity in that month.

title: Add CI check for error_tags
review:
BODY: (empty)
[.github/workflows/error_tags_check.yml] `error_tags_check.yml` не перезапускается при добавлении `ok-to-test`, в отличие от `pr_check.yml`.

В `pr_check` явно указано:

```yaml
types:
  - opened
  - synchronize
  - reopened
  - labeled
```

В `error_tags_check` — только дефолтные события (`opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`), без `labeled`.

**Что ломается:** для внешнего контрибьютора workflow стартует на `opened`, ownership check возвращает `false`, валидация skip'ается. Maintainer ставит `ok-to-test` → `pr_check` сразу перезапускается, а `error_tags_check` — нет, пока автор не сделает новый push.

**Предложение:** добавить `labeled` в `on.pull_request_target.types` (и по аналогии с `pr_check` — concurrency/условие, чтобы irrelevant labels не отменяли running checks).

_2026-05-13_: Filed issue.
_2026-06-08_: Added new findings (16) and (86).

### Bug description

I found 22 free-threading race conditions during a partial Xint Code scan of cpython. These only apply to the free-threaded build, and were all found and tested on commit 0534774a472424f6b9be2dc4ce9784384bc02401 built with `./configure --disable-gil --enable-asan` on an M3 Mac.

I'm attaching a zip file with detailed writeups of each, as well as reproduction cases for 15 of the 22 issues. I don't have scripts reproducing the findings numbered 21, 36, 82, 94, 106, 115, or 124. Race conditions can be difficult to trigger, and even the scripts I provided are trying to win tight races and may not always work.

I know this is a lot. @colesbury suggested I create a combined issue to make the triage discussion easier.

Let me know if you have any questions or concerns. The issues were found and written up by an automated system, but I have put additional work into the validation and reporting. I do want to be respectful of everyone's time while helping to make Python better.

title: feat(spans-buffer): add Redis slowlog logger for debugging
review:
BODY: I am not sure I understand what you would use the SLOWLOG response for. 
SLOWLOG tells you the  list of commands that took the longest in the previous period of time. 
If you want to use this to validate that the flusher is the cause of the CPU spikes, why not record the cumulative time  spent and amount of data extracted by each queue like we do for the cumulative time spent per trace ?
[src/sentry/spans/buffer.py] They would not. SLOWLOG is per Redis host (which means per shard). Actually I don't think calling it from the client will serve any purpose as the host you hit from the client may not be the one that serves the request. redis node can forward requests to other nodes if they do not own the shard that executes the command. 

So you would have to connect specifically to the shard that you are interested into and run the SLOWLOG command on there, otherwise you would be running it on the wrong node.
[src/sentry/spans/buffer_logger.py] I don't think this will do what you want. SLOWLOG is per node on the cluster, not per cluster. It would give different results depending which node you run it onto.

title: Google: Fix false success in Cloud Composer DAG run sensor
review: BODY: This PR looks similar to this one https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/61046 which was reverted because this code broke `CloudComposerDAGRunSensor`. Could you run the existing System Test for this operator and shared the screenshot for the latest run?
request:
[ISSUE apache/airflow#57512 by Git4Vishal] `CloudComposerDAGRunSensor` returns success when no Dag runs found in `execution_range`
### Apache Airflow version

2.11.0

### If "Other Airflow 2/3 version" selected, which one?

_No response_

### What happened?

Summary:
CloudComposerDAGRunSensor incorrectly returns True (success) when no DAG runs exist within the specified execution_range, potentially causing downstream tasks to execute without the expected upstream dependencies being met.



### What you think should happen instead?

The sensor should only return True when:

1. At least one DAG run exists within the execution_range, AND
2. All DAG runs within that range are in allowed_states

If no runs exist in the time window, the sensor should return False (continue waiting).

**Actual Behavior**
The sensor returns True even when no DAG runs exist within the execution_range, causing downstream tasks to proceed without the expected dependency being met.

**Impact**
This bug can cause serious production issues:

1. Silent Data Pipeline Failures: Downstream tasks execute without required upstream data
2. Data Corruption: Tasks process incomplete or missing datasets
3. No Error Alerts: The sensor succeeds silently, providing no indication of the missing dependency
4. Difficult to Debug: The issue only manifests as data inconsistencies, not task failures

**Real-World Scenario**

# Daily ETL pipeline on Astronomer depends on Composer DAG
```python
wait_for_composer = CloudComposerDAGRunSensor(
    composer_dag_id="daily_data_ingestion",
    execution_range=[yesterday_9am, yesterday_5pm],  # Yesterday's business hours
)
```
If the Composer DAG _daily_data_ingestion_ never ran yesterday:

- ❌ Buggy Behavior: Sensor returns True → Downstream ETL proceeds with no data → Data corruption
- ✅ Expected Behavior: Sensor returns False → Keeps waiting → Eventually times out with clear error

### How to reproduce


**Steps to Reproduce**
**1. Create Test DAG**
```python
from airflow.decorators import dag
from airflow.providers.google.cloud.sensors.cloud_composer import CloudComposerDAGRunSensor
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from airflow.utils.dates import days_ago

@dag(schedule_interval=None, start_date=days_ago(1), catchup=False)
def test_composer_sensor_bug():

    # Set up time window where NO runs exist
    yesterday = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=1)
    start_time = datetime(yesterday.year, yesterday.month, yesterday.day, 11, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    end_time = datetime(yesterday.year, yesterday.month, yesterday.day, 14, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

    # Monitor a DAG that has runs, but NONE in the time window
    sensor = CloudComposerDAGRunSensor(
        task_id="test_sensor",
        project_id="my-project",
        region="us-east1",
        environment_id="my-composer-env",
        composer_dag_id="target_dag",  # This DAG exists but didn't run in the window
        execution_range=[start_time, end_time],
        poke_interval=10,
        timeout=60,
    )

test_composer_sensor_bug()
```

**2. Prerequisites**

- A Composer environment with a DAG that has historical runs
- Ensure the target DAG has NO runs within the specified time window
- Example: If checking yesterday 11:00-14:00, ensure the DAG didn't run during that time

**3. Execute DAG**
`
airflow dags trigger test_composer_sensor_bug
`
**4. Observe Buggy Behavior**

- **Expected**: Sensor times out after 60 seconds (no runs in window)
- **Actual**: Sensor immediately succeeds (returns True)

**Root Cause Analysis**
**Buggy Code**
**Location**: _airflow/providers/google/cloud/sensors/cloud_composer.py_
`
def _check_dag_runs_states(
    self,
    dag_runs: list[dict],
    start_date: datetime,
    end_date: datetime,
) -> bool:
    for dag_run in dag_runs:
        if (
            start_date.timestamp()
            < parser.parse(
                dag_run["execution_date" if self._composer_airflow_version < 3 else "logical_date"]
            ).timestamp()
            < end_date.timestamp()
        ) and dag_run["state"] not in self.allowed_states:
            return False
    return True  # ❌ BUG: Returns True even if no runs found in window!
`
**Why It Fails**
**Scenario**: No DAG runs in time window

- dag_runs contains runs, but all are outside the time window
- Loop iterates through all runs
- For each run, the time window check start_date < execution_date < end_date evaluates to False
- The and operator short-circuits, so dag_run["state"] not in self.allowed_states is never evaluated
- Loop never returns False
- Method reaches return True at the end ❌

**Proposed Fix**
**Fixed Code**
```python
def _check_dag_runs_states(
    self,
    dag_runs: list[dict],
    start_date: datetime,
    end_date: datetime,
) -> bool:
    found_runs_in_window = False  # Track if we found any runs

    for dag_run in dag_runs:
        execution_date = parser.parse(
            dag_run["execution_date" if self._composer_airflow_version < 3 else "logical_date"]
        )

        # Check if run is within time window
        if start_date.timestamp() < execution_date.timestamp() < end_date.timestamp():
            found_runs_in_window = True  # Mark that we found at least one run

            # If any run in window is not in allowed states, return False immediately
            if dag_run["state"] not in self.allowed_states:
                return False

    # ✅ FIX: Only return True if we found at least one run in the window
    return found_runs_in_window
```
**Key Changes**

1. Added found_runs_in_window flag: Tracks whether at least one run exists in the time window
2. Separated conditions: Split the compound condition to set the flag independently
3. Conditional return: Only return True if runs were found AND all are in allowed states
4.

The error in the issue is either a race condition in the build where the build is overwriting the compiler inputs, or it is a memory corruption (e.g. GC hole) leading to intermittent crash.

request:
[ISSUE pytorch/pytorch#177372 by Sanskaaar1] Add torch.narrow_scatter operator to complete the *_copy/*_scatter operator family.
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

### The feature, motivation and pitch

PyTorch currently has `narrow_copy` but lacks the corresponding `narrow_scatter` operator, breaking the pattern where every `*_copy` operation has a matching `*_scatter` operation:
- `slice_copy` / `slice_scatter` - exists
- `select_copy` / `select_scatter` - exists
- `narrow_copy` / `narrow_scatter` - missing

Without `narrow_scatter`, the functorch functionalization layer can't properly handle mutations through narrow views. Right now users have to use mutation-based workarounds that don't work with functorch:

```python
# Current workaround (not functional, incompatible with functorch)
result = input.clone()
result.narrow(dim, start, length).copy_(src)
```

I'd like to propose adding `torch.narrow_scatter(input, src, dim, start, length) -> Tensor` which scatters values from `src` into a narrow region of `input`:

```python
import torch

# Basic usage
x = torch.zeros(10)
src = torch.ones(5) * 2
result = torch.narrow_scatter(x, src, dim=0, start=2, length=5)
# tensor([0., 0., 2., 2., 2., 2., 2., 0., 0., 0.])

# Autograd support
x = torch.randn(10, 10, requires_grad=True)
src = torch.randn(5, 10, requires_grad=True)
result = torch.narrow_scatter(x, src, 0, 2, 5)
result.sum().backward()  # gradients computed correctly

# torch.compile support
@torch.compile
def fn(x, src):
    return torch.narrow_scatter(x, src, 0, 2, 5)
```

The implementation can delegate to `slice_scatter` since narrow is just slice with step=1:

```cpp
at::Tensor narrow_scatter_symint(..., SymInt start, SymInt length) {
  c10::SymInt end = start + length;
  return at::slice_scatter_symint(self, src, dim, start, end, 1);
}
```

This keeps the implementation minimal and reuses all existing `slice_scatter` optimizations.


### Alternatives

Users can work around this with `slice_scatter` directly:
```python
result = torch.slice_scatter(input, src, dim, start, start+length, 1)
```

However, this is less intuitive (requires computing `end = start + length`) and inconsistent with the `narrow_copy` naming convention.

The mutation-based workaround also exists but doesn't work with functorch:
```python
result = input.clone()
result.narrow(dim, start, length).copy_(src)
```

### Additional context

[Related PR #175609](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/175609/changes)

[ISSUE ray-project/ray#1234 by suquark] Ray fails to serialize self-reference objects
<!--
General questions should be asked on the mailing list ray-dev@googlegroups.com.

Before submitting an issue, please fill out the following form.
-->

### System information
- **Ray installed from (source or binary)**: pip
- **Ray version**: 0.2.2
- **Python version**: 3.6.2

<!--
You can obtain the Ray version with

python -c "import ray; print(ray.__version__)"
-->

### Describe the problem

Ray fails to serialize self-reference objects (for example, Graph objects in networkx).

I think it is because ray always tries to use pyarrow first and does not catch `pyarrow.lib.ArrowNotImplementedError`, see

https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/e0360eb4298371e308cd266dd512befaa457ce24/python/ray/worker.py#L285-L289

After catching `pyarrow.lib.ArrowNotImplementedError`, we **should not** use `use_dict=True` as a workaround, because it will cause endless loop. A correct approach may be:

```python
            except (pyarrow.SerializationCallbackError, pyarrow.lib.ArrowNotImplementedError) as e:
                try:
                    if isinstance(e, pyarrow.lib.ArrowNotImplementedError):
                        e.example_object = value
                        raise e  # redirect to use cloudpickle
```

### Source code / logs
<!-- Include any logs or source code that would be helpful to diagnose the problem. If including tracebacks, please include the full traceback. Large logs and files should be attached. Try to provide a reproducible test case that is the bare minimum necessary to generate the problem. -->

```python
class Graph:
    def __init__(self):
        self.g = self

G = Graph()
ray.put(G)  # --> pyarrow.lib.ArrowNotImplementedError: This object exceeds the maximum recursion depth. It may contain itself recursively.

# another example

import networkx as nx
G = nx.Graph()
    
G.add_edges_from([(1, 2), (1, 3)])
G.add_node(1)
G.add_edge(1, 2)
G.add_node("spam")  # adds node "spam"
G.add_nodes_from("spam")  # adds 4 nodes: 's', 'p', 'a', 'm'
G.add_edge(3, 'm')
ray.put(G)  # --> pyarrow.lib.ArrowNotImplementedError: This object exceeds the maximum recursion depth. It may contain itself recursively.
```

@mitar 
[ISSUE COMMENT by robertnishihara] Can you try `ray.register_custom_serializer`? The following works for me.

```python
import ray
ray.init()

class Graph:
    def __init__(self):
        self.g = self

ray.register_custom_serializer(Graph, use_pickle=True)

G = Graph()
ray.put(G)
```

This is closely related to #319 and https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/ARROW-1382.

A side comment. The original code worked for me in Python 2 because in Python 2 `Graph` is an old-style class and so we automatically fall back to Pickle anyway I think.
[ISSUE COMMENT by mitar] Hm, so ideally we would like to serialize networkx graphs. Because they can be quite large, I am not sure if pickling is a good approach.
[ISSUE COMMENT by robertnishihara] Custom serializers/deserializers can be registered with the same approach. Not sure what the right one would be in this case, but just as a simple example, you could do something like

```python
import numpy as np
import ray

ray.init()

class Graph:
    def __init__(self, big_array):
        self.g = self
        self.big_array = big_array

def custom_graph_serializer(obj):
    return obj.big_array

def custom_graph_deserializer(serialized_obj):
    return Graph(serialized_obj)

ray.register_custom_serializer(Graph,
                               serializer=custom_graph_serializer,
                               deserializer=custom_graph_deserializer)

G = Graph(np.ones(100))
ray.put(G)

title: [hotwired__turbo] Align types with the v8.0.23 implementation
review:
BODY: can you break these changes up to make it easier to review? it feels like you've got a few different types of changes in this

fwiw I also purposely have been taking a "just-in-time" approach w/ filling out these types to make it easier to maintain and confirm what types should be based on the real world behaviours, and so far that seems to be going ok based on how few PRs and issues we've had - I'm not against attempting to backfill types like this, but I'm not sure how valuable it is to be going through the implementation line by line 🤷
request:
[ISSUE DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped#75207 by myabc] [hotwired__turbo] `StreamMessage` and `BrowserAdapter` are declared as value exports but do not exist at runtime
🤖 _Drafted with agent assistance._

While auditing `types/hotwired__turbo` against the Turbo source (hotwired/turbo @ v8.0.23), I found two declarations that claim runtime values which `@hotwired/turbo` does not actually export:

- **`StreamMessage`** — declared as `export class StreamMessage` with a constructor and static members (`wrap`, `contentType`). Turbo only uses this class internally; it is not re-exported from `src/core/index.js` nor from the package entry point (`src/index.js`).
- **`BrowserAdapter`** — declared as `export class BrowserAdapter`; also internal-only (lives in `src/core/native/browser_adapter.js`, never re-exported).

I verified against the built `dist/turbo.es2017-esm.js` export list (32 exports) — neither name is present.

Consequence: the following compiles cleanly against our types but fails at runtime, because both imports resolve to `undefined`:

```ts
import { BrowserAdapter, StreamMessage } from "@hotwired/turbo";

const message = new StreamMessage(fragment); // TypeError at runtime
StreamMessage.wrap("<turbo-stream>…</turbo-stream>"); // TypeError at runtime
```

Our own `hotwired__turbo-tests.ts` exercises exactly these patterns (`new StreamMessage(...)`, `StreamMessage.wrap(...)`, importing `BrowserAdapter`), so the tests currently encode the phantom API.

Options I see:

1. **Demote to types-only.** Make `StreamMessage` and `BrowserAdapter` interfaces (plus a separate type for the statics if we want to keep describing them). Breaking for anyone value-importing them — but that code is already broken at runtime, so arguably this is the fix. The existing `adapter as BrowserAdapter` cast for `progressBar` access keeps working with an interface.
2. **Fix upstream first.** Propose that hotwired/turbo exports `StreamMessage` (and possibly `BrowserAdapter`). `renderStreamMessage()` accepts a `StreamMessage` and `StreamMessage.contentType` is useful for `Accept` headers, so a runtime export seems defensible. Our declarations would then become truthful as-is.
3. **Both**: demote now, restore the class declarations if/when upstream exports them.

Related context on alignment philosophy: https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/pull/75196#discussion_r3509421777

cc @G-Rath @lukeify
